text:
carla: Team, heads-up: we got an invoice from WeWorksoft GmbH (DE) charging 19% VAT on a software integration billed to Redwood Svenska AB. Sales says the contract is B2B — can tax confirm if reverse-charge applies or whether vendor should be using OSS?

carla: Invoice snippet:
```
Invoice: WWS-2026-559
Vendor: WeWorksoft GmbH, DE123456789
Customer: Redwood Svenska AB, VAT SE556677889901
Description: SaaS integration + remote config (May 2026)
Net: 12,000
VAT (19%): 2,280
Total: 14,280
```

sven-vendor: Hi, Sven from WeWorksoft. Our accounting auto-applies German VAT unless buyer supplies VAT ID at time of order. We're registered for OSS for some digital supplies and unsure which rule fits here. Can Redwood provide buyer VAT and confirm B2B so we can reissue? We typically don't credit VAT after payment unless reissue issued.

sarah: Tax: Place-of-supply for B2B services (consulting/integration) is the customer's establishment (Article 44/196 of the EU VAT Directive). If the buyer is an EU VAT-registered business and VIES validates the VAT ID, the supplier should apply reverse charge (0% on invoice, include buyer VAT, and reference "reverse charge / article 196 VAT Directive"). OSS is for supplies to non-taxable persons (B2C) and would require charging VAT at customer country rates. So OSS is not the right path for a B2B transaction.

mike: Sales confirms PO to Redwood Svenska AB. Lina attaching PO and the customer's VAT that we have on file.

lina-sales: Attached: PO-90077.pdf and buyer VAT SE556677889901. Customer confirms they're B2B. Attaching VIES screenshot too.

invoicebot: Invoice WWS-2026-559 uploaded to NetSuite. Flag: VAT_MISMATCH_HOLD.

sven-vendor: Ok we'll reissue if you confirm VIES. Quick Q: our OSS registration covers digital goods — this was a hybrid services bundle. Will finance accept a vendor note plus VIES screenshot or do you need a fully reissued invoice?

sarah: Prefer a reissued invoice without German VAT showing buyer VAT SE556677889901 and the line: "Reverse charge - article 196 VAT Directive. Buyer liable for VAT." If vendor cannot reissue quickly, we can accept a vendor-signed certificate + VIES screenshot for audit to release payment, but reissue is cleaner for bookkeeping. No gross-up — we won't reimburse VAT charged if vendor refuses to correct (we'd reclaim through VAT return which is slower).

eva-legal: Legal note: invoice should also include vendor VAT number and a brief description of the service. For audit, we need either (A) replacement invoice referencing reverse charge or (B) signed written confirmation from vendor that supply is B2B + buyer VAT + VIES validation. If vendor insists OSS, ask them to explain why they think the supply is B2C and provide evidence of consumer end-users — otherwise it's misapplication of OSS.

sven-vendor: Understood. We'll reissue a corrected invoice by COB with buyer VAT and reverse charge reference. If our accounting refuses, we'll send a signed statement certifying buyer VAT and that services are business-to-business.

carla: Finance action: hold payment until corrected invoice or vendor certificate + VIES screenshot. Tax: once doc received, please update NetSuite and remove VAT_MISMATCH_HOLD. Save evidence to /finance/vat-audit/2026/weworksoft.

mike: I'll confirm with the account team that all work was delivered to the Swedish entity (not a UK or DE establishment).

sarah: One more thing: ensure the invoice references the PO number and buyer registration as that helps our ledger mapping.

sven-vendor: Will include PO reference and buyer VAT. Thanks.

carla: Closing once reissued invoice or certificate is uploaded. :white_check_mark:
